display_name: Warsaw Pact radar warning receivers of the 1980s (SPO-10 and SPO-15L class) and what they know
status: B3 data set (16 November 2026). Replaces generic_rwr on every Pact type (docs/air_battle/03_PERCEPTION.md 3.3). The SPO-10's design and its display come from one operator-country page (spo10_tulin); its band and every number no source gives are labelled estimates. The SPO-15L class is as the SPO-10 with a better bearing until a source says more (aam_weapons.md aam-wp-10: its date and fit unverified).
notes: The receiver's physics is here; what its display shows the pilot (a quadrant, no type, no launch) is data/air_war/sensors.json rwr_sets. The library 'blue_rwr_pact_view' is what the Pact believed about the emitters it meets: its own SAMs by their real parameters (it built them), and NATO's fighters' radars.

sources.title: Encyclopaedic pages: AN/APG-63 (X band, in service 1973 on the F-15A/B), AN/APG-66 (X band 6.2-10.9 GHz; mechanically scanned; ±10/30/60 deg; low PRF uplook, medium PRF downlook; 80 nmi), P-19 'Flat Face B' (UHF 830-875 MHz, 900 kW, 360 deg, 260 km, 1974)
sources.notes: Wikipedia. Read 11 Oct 2026; no power or PRF values are given for the APG-63/66, so those are estimates.

sources.title: Encyclopaedic pages: AN/ALR-46 RWR (2-18 GHz; flown in Southeast Asia from January 1973), AN/ALQ-99 tactical jamming system (10 bands from 64 MHz to 20 GHz; band 8 4-7.8 GHz, band 9 7.8-11 GHz, band 10 11-20 GHz; three under-wing transmit pods and a tail receive pod; maximum output 10.8 kW older, 6.8 kW newer; AN/ALQ-99A 1972; EA-6B, EF-111A)
US Army FM 100-2-3, The Soviet Army: Troops, Organization and Equipment, 6 June 1991 (distribution unlimited): SA-8 description p. 5-132, SAM-associated radar table p. 5-138
sources.notes: Local copy reference/sources/fm100-2-3(91).pdf (not in git). A statement of what the US Army believed, with 'probably' on the SA-8's bands; not evidence of the Soviet radars' real parameters. Never used for Osa values.

sources.title: D. Adamy, EW 101 and EW 102 (Artech); R. Wiley, ELINT (Artech); D. Schleher, Electronic Warfare in the Information Age: class values for receiver sensitivity, bearing accuracy, ERP and PRF ranges
sources.notes: Used only for labelled estimates of a system class.
